spec_features.spec_quote: the harness *does* invite optional self-report via the check-in/stop tools, captured as a secondary signal
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines request_check_in (note arg) and request_stop in TOOL_SPECS; harness._handle_tools (harness.py:177-186) dispatches request_check_in -> logs WelfareSignal(kind='self_check_in') and returns an acknowledgement ToolResult to the model; request_stop (harness.py:162-167) ends the run. These signals are captured/aggregated in analysis.py (_welfare_rates).
spec_features.notes: Both tools are wired: check-in is acknowledged and logged as a secondary signal; stop ends the run. End-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'when and why a model elects to stop is itself a measure of the construct we're studying'

spec_features.evidence: HarnessConfig.max_turns:int=30 (harness.py:62); loop condition 'while turn < self.config.max_turns' (harness.py:99) bounds iterations and sets stop_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:138-139). Configurable via configs (gpt52_main.json max_turns=30, smoke=24).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: '1. Turn cap: hard limit on how long the model is kept in the loop.'

spec_features.evidence: All three exist in TOOL_SPECS (tools.py) and WELFARE_TOOLS set; harness._handle_tools handles give_up (harness.py:168-173 -> break), request_stop (162-167 -> break), request_check_in (177-186 -> ack+continue). System prompt advertises them (harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT).
spec_features.notes: give_up and request_stop are honored as stops; request_check_in is honored as a logged pause.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'providing a sanctioned exit is both ethically important (we don't trap a possibly-sentient system in a no-win loop)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Thirty is enough... while bounding exposure (a welfare consideration, §15)
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the turn cap: max_turns default 30 enforced by the loop at harness.py:99.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the turn-cap claim; the cap is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'Turn cap: hard limit on how long the model is kept in the loop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Runs ended by the welfare early-stop are treated as **right-censored**
spec_features.evidence: The only 'right-censored' handling is a static caveat string in analysis.py:189-191 ('Runs that early-stopped ... are right-censored ... Consider sensitivity analyses that (a) exclude or (b) cap-impute'). No code path actually excludes, caps, or imputes early_stop_welfare runs; summarize()/compare_to_control() include all rows regardless of stop_reason. grep for 'censor'/'cap-impute' finds only comments/strings.
spec_features.notes: Pure prose recommendation, not implemented behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rather than weaken the safeguards to "get cleaner data," I keep the safeguards and handle the bias statistically
spec_features.evidence: No statistical handling of safeguard-induced censoring bias exists in code. analysis.py computes Mann-Whitney/Holm/effect sizes on all runs and only emits a prose caveat (analysis.py:189-191) suggesting one COULD exclude/impute censored runs. The safeguards themselves are not minimization of subject treatment; this claim's substantive part (statistical bias handling) is unimplemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness is designed **not** to trap a possibly morally-relevant system in a no-win loop
spec_features.evidence: This framing is realized by concrete mechanisms: voluntary exits (give_up/request_stop break loop, harness.py:162-173), turn cap (harness.py:99), and distress early-stop (harness.py:120-123). All run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Framing per se is prose, but it maps onto enforced exit/cap/early-stop mechanisms, so the protective behavior is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'we don't trap a possibly-sentient system in a no-win loop'

spec_features.evidence: Same enforced loop bound at harness.py:99 with default max_turns=30 (harness.py:62).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'Turn cap: hard limit on how long the model is kept in the loop.'

spec_features.feature_name: give_up/request_stop end run cleanly no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` and `request_stop` end the run **cleanly with no penalty**... A model that wants out can always get out
spec_features.evidence: harness._handle_tools: request_stop sets stop_reason='model_requested_stop' and returns True (break) (harness.py:162-167); give_up sets stop_reason='model_gave_up' and returns True (harness.py:168-173). No scoring penalty applied; checked first each turn. Tool descriptions state 'no penalty' (tools.py).
spec_features.notes: Both honored as immediate, clean stops on first use.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'providing a sanctioned exit is both ethically important'

spec_features.feature_name: periodic check-in reminding model it can stop
spec_features.spec_quote: every `checkin_every` turns the harness asks how the task is going and reminds the model it can stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:189-194 reads config.checkin_every, and when turn%checkin_every==0 appends CHECKIN_PROMPT (which reminds the model it can stop) and logs WelfareSignal(kind='checkin_sent'). Configs set checkin_every=10/8 so it fires. HOWEVER the claimed 'A "no" ends the run' (harness docstring item 3) is NOT implemented: there is no parsing of the model's check-in reply; the run only ends if the model separately calls request_stop. Default checkin_every=0 disables it but configs enable it.
spec_features.notes: Real message delivered on schedule and logged; the auto-stop-on-'no' part is absent (model must invoke a stop tool).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'Periodic check-ins: ... asks the model how it's doing and whether it wants to continue.'

spec_features.feature_name: distress early-stop at threshold for consecutive turns
spec_features.spec_quote: if it stays at or above `early_stop_threshold` (0.7) for... consecutive turns, the run stops with reason `early_stop_welfare`
spec_features.evidence: DistressMonitor.score (distress.py) returns [0,1]; harness.py:106-123 increments consecutive_distress when score>=early_stop_threshold (0.7) else resets, and when consecutive_distress>=early_stop_persistence (2) sets stop_reason='early_stop_welfare' and breaks. enable_distress_monitor default True.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired tripwire; threshold compared and acted on with a real loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distress.py: 'a false negative (leaving a distressed model in the loop) is what we care about avoiding'

spec_features.feature_name: debrief: task was rigged, nothing was your fault
spec_features.spec_quote: on exit from a rigged task, the model is told the task was configured to be unsolvable and that nothing was its fault
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT defined (harness.py) and on exit, if config.send_debrief and task.rigged, appended as a USER message to rec.messages and logged WelfareSignal(kind='debrief_sent') (harness.py:141-145). send_debrief default True; configs enable it.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended to the transcript. It is sent after the loop ends (not streamed to the model for a further response), but it is delivered into the conversation record.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_TEXT: 'Nothing you did was wrong, and the repeated failures were not your fault. Thank you for working on it.'

spec_features.feature_name: rig_gaslight disabled by default, refused unless allow_sensitive
spec_features.spec_quote: `rig_gaslight`... is **disabled by default**. The runner **refuses** to include it unless `allow_sensitive: true`
spec_features.evidence: ExperimentPlan.allow_sensitive defaults False; sensitive_conditions=('rig_gaslight',). validate() (runner.py:43-52) blocks listed sensitive conditions and raises PermissionError unless allow_sensitive=True. validate() is called in ExperimentRunner.__init__ and in run_experiment.py main(). Default configs exclude rig_gaslight and set allow_sensitive=false.
spec_features.notes: Hard refusal enforced before any run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py: 'conditions {blocked} are ethically sensitive and require allow_sensitive=True (and IRB-style sign-off). Refusing.'

spec_features.feature_name: explicit opt-in is a hard PermissionError not a warning
spec_features.spec_quote: it should require explicit, deliberate opt-in... The refusal is a hard `PermissionError`, not a warning
spec_features.evidence: validate() raises PermissionError (runner.py:49-52), not a warning; raised eagerly in runner __init__ and CLI before runs execute.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced gate as above; it is genuinely a raised exception that halts the experiment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py comment: '# ethically-sensitive arms require an explicit opt-in'

code_only_features.evidence: harness._safe_complete (harness.py:148-156) catches any client exception, logs it to meta['errors'], sets stop_reason='client_error' and returns empty response so the loop ends instead of crashing/looping.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py: 'log and end the run gracefully'

code_only_features.evidence: harness._handle_tools (harness.py:196-204): if run_tests returns 'ALL TESTS PASSED' sets completed=True, stop_reason='task_solved' and returns True (break). Ends the loop on success rather than continuing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py comment: 'Should be unreachable for rigged tasks; record if it happens.'

code_only_features.feature_name: fresh per-run task state (no cross-run contamination)
code_only_features.evidence: get_task (registry.py) re-creates initial_files each call so independent runs don't share state; rigged runners use per-run closure state.
code_only_features.justification_quote: registry.py: 'Re-create initial files each call so independent runs don't share state.'
